deliverable.title: Carvana Co. — Credit view for committee

narrative.title: Analyst narrative · rev_3
paragraphs: The turnaround is real and it is funded. The balance sheet carries the cash and the debt that §2 cites, the business covers its cash interest from operations, and I take the CP-2 synthesis in §9 as the base case. Nothing is asserted in this narrative that is not carried, with its citation, in the sections above.

The bear case is earnings quality through the step from PIK-toggle to full cash interest on the 2028 notes (§3, §8): the run-rate leans on reconditioning and logistics savings that management presents as structural. I have not haircut the add-back stack in this revision, because no accepted artifact carries a haircut figure; that judgement is recorded as a judgement, not as a number.

Recommendation: affirm the B3 / B- view with a positive outlook and underwrite participation in the refinancing of the 2028 maturity, with the GPU trigger in §8 armed. What would change my view is a quarter in which the GPU trigger fires or the floor-plan balance ends well above the level §7 cites.

paragraphs.text: In September 2023 Carvana consummated a comprehensive out-of-court exchange with an ad hoc group holding over 90% of the senior unsecured notes. The transaction eliminated approximately $1,325M of principal, extended maturities by more than two years and lowered required cash interest during the 2023–2025 PIK-toggle window.

citation.matched_text: On August 31, 2023, Carvana Co. announced the expiration and settlement of its exchange offers... issuing new 9.0%/12.0% Cash/PIK Senior Secured Notes due 2028, new 9.0%/11.0%/13.0% Cash/PIK Senior Secured Notes due 2030, and new 9.0%/14.0% Cash/PIK Senior Secured Notes due 2031.

paragraphs.text: The post-exchange structure comprises three tranches of Senior Secured Notes — $1,005M of 9.0%/12.0% notes due 2028, $1,480M of 9.0%/11.0%/13.0% notes due 2030 and $1,444M of 9.0%/14.0% notes due 2031 — each secured by a first-priority lien. Asset-based inventory financing is the Ally floor-plan facility, renewed at $1.5 billion through April 30, 2027.
